# COI Journal

> A publication about construction insurance compliance: contractor certificates of insurance (COIs), endorsements, project requirements and who pays when coverage fails. Published by Forsured (https://forsured.ai), a construction insurance compliance software company. COI Journal does not rank or review software vendors.

## Articles

- [Why we're starting COI Journal](https://coijournal.com/articles/why-coi-journal/index.md): COI Journal is a new publication on construction insurance compliance, published by Forsured. What we'll cover, what we won't, and how we'll earn your trust.

## About the publication

- [About COI Journal](https://coijournal.com/about/): COI Journal reports on construction insurance compliance: contractor COIs, endorsements and project requirements. Published by Forsured. Here's why and how.
- [The COI Digest](https://coijournal.com/digest/): The COI Digest is COI Journal's weekly email: Worth Reading, our picks of the week's best COI reporting, plus one term and one gap. Tuesdays.
- [Gap of the Month](https://coijournal.com/gap-of-the-month/): Tell COI Journal about a contractor insurance gap that caught you out. We pick one a month, explain it, and credit you only if you want.
- [Methodology and the COI Gap Index](https://coijournal.com/methodology/): How COI Journal research is built: where the data comes from, how it's anonymized, and the minimum sample sizes behind every number we publish.
- [Publishing principles](https://coijournal.com/principles/): How COI Journal reports: ownership disclosure, sourcing, corrections, how we cover competitors, and the line between editorial and Forsured's business.

## The COI Dictionary

- [Certificate of insurance (COI)](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/certificate-of-insurance/): A one-page summary of a contractor's insurance at the moment it was issued. In construction it is almost always the ACORD 25, the Certificate of Liability Insurance.
- [Additional insured (AI)](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/additional-insured/): A person or company added to someone else's liability policy, usually the owner and the general contractor on a trade contractor's policy. Status comes from an endorsement, not from the certificate.
- [Completed operations](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/completed-operations/): Liability for injury or damage that shows up after a contractor's work is finished, such as a leak or a collapse months after turnover. For an additional insured, it usually needs its own endorsement.
- [Primary and noncontributory](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/primary-and-noncontributory/): Wording that makes the contractor's policy pay first for the additional insured, without asking the additional insured's own policy to share the loss.
- [Waiver of subrogation](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/waiver-of-subrogation/): A promise by the contractor's insurer not to sue you to recover what it paid on a claim. Construction contracts usually require it on general liability, auto and workers' compensation.
- [Per project aggregate](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/per-project-aggregate/): An endorsement that gives each construction project its own general aggregate limit, so claims on one job can't use up the limit for yours.
- [Notice of cancellation](https://coijournal.com/dictionary/notice-of-cancellation/): Advance notice that a contractor's policy is being cancelled. The certificate itself doesn't promise to tell you.
